articles.headline: Zack Wheeler fans 7 straight to open Phillies win over Brewers
articles.description: Zack Wheeler struck out 11, including seven in a row to start the game, and Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking single with two outs in the eighth inning as the Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4 victory over the Brewers.
articles.headlineJa: ザック・ウィーラーが初回から7者連続三振、フィリーズがブルワーズを下す
articles.descriptionJa: ザック・ウィーラーが試合開始からの7者連続を含む11奪三振を記録し、8回2死からブライソン・ストットが勝ち越し打を放って、フィリーズが6-4でブルワーズに勝利し、プレーオフ進出確定へと一歩近づきました。
articles.body:
Zack Wheeler struck out 11, including seven in a row to start the game, and Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking single with two outs in the eighth inning as the Philadelphia Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night.

Wheeler reached 2,000 career strikeouts when he fanned Brice Turang to end the first, becoming the 96th pitcher in MLB history to reach the milestone.

"Just being where I am now, it's pretty special," Wheeler said of the career milestone, according to MLB.com. "It's a huge thank you to all the catchers that I've had along the way that helped me get here, the coaches and the guys that played behind me. It means a lot to me, and I really appreciate everybody's effort around it."

Unhittable at the outset, Wheeler had sights on Pablo López's MLB record of nine strikeouts in a row to open a contest before Cooper Pratt grounded out to third base for the second out of the third inning.

"I didn't know what to expect coming out," Wheeler said. "Just one of those days for me."

Wheeler is the only Phillies pitcher since 1900 with seven straight strikeouts to start a game, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. Watching Wheeler from the dugout was teammate Aaron Nola, who has a share of the MLB record with 10 consecutive strikeouts of the New York Mets in 2021.

Brandon Marsh homered, doubled and drove in three runs for Philadelphia, which is tied with the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres at 87-70 for the three National League wild cards -- four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks with five to play. The Phillies hold a tiebreaker over the Padres but not the Cubs.

William Contreras had three RBIs for NL Central champion Milwaukee. The Brewers, by virtue of Cincinnati's 4-0 win over Atlanta, clinched a bye in the wild-card round and earned home-field advantage for the division series. The Brewers dropped to 13-6 this month and were not able to extend their franchise record of 98 wins, set in Sunday's 3-0 victory at Baltimore.

After the Brewers scored twice in the sixth inning off Wheeler to tie the game at 3, Stott singled to center off Colton Gordon (0-1). Garrett Mitchell's throw went to third base to try to get Alec Bohm running from first, but the ball ricocheted off Bohm's foot and both he and Luis Arraez scored to make it 5-3.

Jhoan Duran earned his 33rd save after Jose Alvarado (5-3) got the final out of the eighth.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks set for surgery, IR move
articles.description: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is expected to undergo surgery to repair a core muscle injury and is set to miss at least six weeks, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズRBジョナソン・ブルックス、手術とIR入りへ（関係者情報）
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークが関係者の話として報じたところによると、パンサーズのランニングバック（RB）ジョナソン・ブルックスは体幹筋肉の損傷を修復する手術を受ける見込みで、少なくとも6週間離脱する予定です。
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is expected to undergo surgery Wednesday to repair a core muscle injury and is set to miss at least six weeks, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Brooks will be placed on injured reserve, sources said.

The running back left Sunday's 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth quarter with what the team called a groin injury. Brooks also dealt with a groin issue in the leadup to the season opener against the Chicago Bears.

Brooks, a second-round pick in the 2024 NFL draft, has played in only five career NFL games after undergoing back-to-back right ACL surgeries.

He had rushed nine times for 30 yards during the Panthers' first two games this season, with Chuba Hubbard taking the majority of the rushing workload (22 carries, 102 yards, 1 touchdown).

articles.headline: Full final 2026 regular-season grades for all 30 MLB teams
articles.description: Whether your team is headed to October or packing its bags for the offseason, how did 2026 measure up to expectations?
articles.headlineJa: MLB全30球団の2026年レギュラーシーズン最終採点
articles.descriptionJa: 応援するチームが10月のポストシーズンに向かうのか、それともオフシーズンを迎えるのかにかかわらず、2026年シーズンは期待通りの結果となったでしょうか？
articles.body:
As we wrap up the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season, it's time for some final grades.

As expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers challenged the single-season record for wins. The New York Mets had a huge offseason that paid off with the National League East title. The New York Yankees dominated the American League East. The Milwaukee Brewers failed to scrap their way to the playoffs. Tarik Skubal carried the Detroit Tigers to the AL Central championship. The Chicago White Sox? A joke once again.

Wait ... no, that's not at all what happened. The only joke -- outside of the usual ineptitude we see from the clubs at the bottom of the majors -- was the AL West, which might see a team with a losing record capture the division title.

The 2026 season might not have gone as expected, but we still had breakout performances, surprising teams, unpredictable results, a flamethrowing phenom, a season for the ages and a very mediocre AL. Let's go to the grades.

Milwaukee Brewers: A+

What a wonderful, engaging and thrilling regular season for the Brewers. They've already set the franchise record for wins in a single season, breaking last year's mark of 97, and are heading to the top record in the majors for the second year in a row. Jacob Misiorowski has been the best individual story of the season -- alongside division rival Pete Crow-Armstrong -- but it has been an impressive teamwide effort.

Milwaukee's rookie pitchers have started 77 games, most in the majors, while another pair of rookies in shortstop Cooper Pratt and right fielder Luis Lara will be starting in October. Brice Turang's 6.9 bWAR is second among MLB position players, and he should finish in the top five of the MVP voting. Oh, and the bullpen is top five in the majors in win probability added.

Not bad for a team that was 11th in ESPN's preseason power rankings. At least we got "the thing we'll be talking about most this season" right for Milwaukee: Misiorowski's sophomore year.

Tampa Bay Rays: A+

Nope, the Rays never faded. In fact, they went 18-10 in August and are 14-6 in September after clinching the division (and the top record in the AL) with a win over the Yankees on Tuesday.

Tampa Bay has been a little hard to analyze at times as it has gone 25-14 in one-run games, which helps erase its 22-23 record in blowout games decided by five-plus. (Good teams almost always have a winning record in blowout games, so this is a weird anomaly.) While Junior Caminero has been a standout and Jonathan Aranda is closing in on 100 RBIs, it's been a year of unsung heroes: Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen lead the rotation with 15 wins apiece and sub 3.00 ERAs; Griffin Jax transitioned from reliever to starter; Bryan Baker leads the majors in saves; Victor Mesa Jr. added surprising power in the second half.

You can ask the same question about the Brewers and the Rays: Will this be the year?

Atlanta Braves: A

Erling Haaland is contracted to Manchester City for another eight years, but could Bayern Munich sign him? Plus, Manchester United have identified a new potential replacement for left back Luke Shaw.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich have emerged as suitors for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, according to TEAMtalk. The Bundesliga side are believed to see the 26-year-old as a potential future replacement for Harry Kane, who they want to remain at the Allianz Arena for a further two years before assessing whether a move for Haaland is possible. Meanwhile, TEAMtalk reports that Vincent Kompany's side are also keen on Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, and could be contenders for his signature next summer amid plans to add him to their squad with England compatriot Kane.

- Liverpool and Manchester United are interested in Crystal Palace defender Tyrick Mitchell, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils reportedly see the 27-year-old as an alternative to Newcastle's Lewis Hall as they continue plans to identify a long-term successor to Luke Shaw. Mitchell entered the final 12 months of his contract in the summer, and it is said that Chelsea are also monitoring his situation, attracted to the opportunity of landing him on a free transfer.

- Chelsea and Manchester City are exploring a move for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda, according to TEAMtalk. The Blues are said to have tracked the 19-year-old for some time, and they are monitoring whether an opportunity to land him could arise due to a lack of minutes for the Rossoneri since returning from his loan spell at Lecce. Camarda scored one goal in 21 Serie A appearances last season.

- Napoli are struggling to make progress in talks with the representatives of midfielder Kevin De Bruyne over a new contract, transfer journalist Nicolo Schira reports. Discussions have reportedly stalled with the 35-year-old, who arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on a two-year deal in the summer of 2025, and it is now said that they are "on the verge" of parting ways next summer. De Bruyne was previously linked with clubs in Major League Soccer and the Saudi Pro League before deciding to join Gli Azzurri.

- On-loan Aston Villa winger Alejandro Garnacho is attracting interest from clubs in LaLiga, the Daily Mail reports. The 22-year-old is believed to be on the radar of several clubs in Spain amid struggles to earn a place in Unai Emery's side, with 32 minutes of action in the Premier League spread across three substitute appearances. articles.descriptionJa: レブロン、ステフ、KDの順位は妥当だったのか？NBAの内部関係者が、今年のランキングにおける最大の選外、サプライズ、そして予測について詳しく解説します。
articles.body:
ESPN continues its countdown of the top 100 players entering the 2026-27 NBA season after rolling out 50-11 today and 100-51 on Monday.

LeBron James, Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant continue their reign near the top of NBA rank as some of the longest-tenured players in the league. But what new faces made their debut?

Before we reveal the top 10 best players in the league, our expert panel breaks down this year's list, answering the biggest questions on surprise snubs and who's up next to break through the rankings.

LeBron James' No. 18 ranking is _____.

Jamal Collier: Questionable. What's the argument for LeBron still being ranked several spots behind the other "old guys" of his generation -- Curry, Durant or Kawhi Leonard?

LeBron carried the Los Angeles Lakers to a playoff series win last year with Luka Doncic injured and Austin Reaves out for most of the series against the Houston Rockets. Injured or not, Durant hasn't won a playoff series since 2023. Curry is still the engine for the Golden State Warriors but didn't get out of the play-in tournament and has played fewer games than LeBron. Leonard is coming off one of the best regular seasons of his career, but he's far from reliable from a health perspective.

LeBron transitioned into a new role with the Lakers and, after an adjustment period, excelled. It might take some time for everyone to adjust in Philly, but James has continued to be as consistent a bet as nearly everyone ahead of him.

Tim MacMahon: Fair. At the ripe age of 41, he's still a legitimate All-Star, which is an unprecedented feat in NBA history. But James is a cut below All-NBA-caliber at this point in his legendary career. He's no longer capable of being the best player on a championship contender, but there has never been a better bargain on a veterans minimum contract.

Anthony Slater: A hint at both the talent glut and offensive challenges ahead for the Sixers. James is behind two of his younger teammates in this rank. Tyrese Maxey (No. 11) is exploding into his prime, and Jaylen Brown (No. 14) is coming off a top-six MVP finish. James had to rearrange his game to take a supplementary role last season next to Doncic and Reaves (when both were healthy). Finding that sweet spot when sharing the floor with Maxey and Brown will define Philadelphia's season.

Brian Windhorst: Appropriate. After the All-Star break last season, LeBron shot 54% and averaged seven rebounds and seven assists while having the lowest usage rate of his career. He morphed midyear into one of the best transition scorers in the league and an off-ball cutter. Had he played five more games and gotten to 65, he very well could have made the All-NBA team.

Collier: Tyrese Haliburton at No. 19 is too low. Haliburton played like a top 10 player during the 2025 playoffs, and he has had more than enough time to recover from an Achilles tear. His regular-season stats might not be as gaudy as some of the guys ah

articles.headline: How San Diego Padres have become a flashpoint in MLB's labor battle
articles.description: Is San Diego why baseball needs a salary cap -- or a shining example of why it doesn't? It depends who you ask.
articles.headlineJa: サンディエゴ・パドレスはどのようにしてMLBの労使対立における争点となったのか
articles.descriptionJa: サンディエゴは野球界にサラリーキャップが必要な理由の象徴なのか、それとも不要であることを示す好例なのか？それは誰に尋ねるかによって意見が分かれます。
articles.body:
ON THE DAY the San Diego Padres' new ownership group was introduced, Manny Machado did some quick math. When the team was sold in 2012, he noted, the purchase price was $800 million. Fourteen years later, the franchise had sold for $3.9 billion -- nearly five times the amount.

"In my business, I wish I could do that investment," said Machado, the Padres' star third baseman. "That's a great return."

At a time when Major League Baseball is attempting to upend its economic model by instituting a salary cap, the Padres have emerged as a beacon for players and union officials who believe a level playing field can exist without one.

In their minds, the Padres' late owner, Peter Seidler, provided the blueprint -- by pouring money into a small-market franchise, elevating the roster to championship contention, turning the ballpark into a destination spot and, after his death, netting a record sale price. Seidler might have absorbed losses along the way, but, in their minds, it was worth it. His peers, they believe, could and should follow.

To others, particularly those who pine for a cap-and-floor system in a new collective bargaining agreement, that rationale is incomplete.

They see the Padres as an outlier and a cautionary tale. Their sale price was inflated as a Southern California franchise in a one-sport town. Their trajectory -- spending so high that a loan was needed for liquidity, a generational talent in Juan Soto traded for the purpose of getting under the luxury tax threshold, a barren farm system and an unsustainable payroll -- is the plight of a team unable to hang with bigger spenders in an open market. Even if other franchises wanted to follow in the Padres' footsteps, they can't, league officials and rival owners argue because their situation is unique.

MLB and the MLB Players' Association are in the midst of a contentious labor fight, and the Padres have become a convenient symbol for both sides. Of inspiration or caution. Of business acumen or reckless spending. Of the possibilities under a free-market system or the pitfalls that come with one.

"You can say it's unique, you can say it's not," said Padres infielder Jake Cronenworth, a member of the MLBPA's executive subcommittee. "But every club has the ability to do what we did -- invest in a good product on the field, invest in the community, and see what happens."

TODAY'S PADRES WOULD be unrecognizable to the 2019 iteration. That team ranked 24th in payroll and ultimately missed the playoffs for a 13th consecutive year.

"No one wanted to play here," said Machado, who joined the team that spring. "We were in the bottom tier of organizations."

The following year, in November 2020, Seidler assumed full control of the Padres, taking over as chairman after his business partner, Ron Fowler, stepped down. Over the next three years, the payroll jumped from $180 million to $225 million to more than $250 million by 2023, trailing only the New York Yankees and New York Mets.

The Padres

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026, players Nos. 50-11: Where LeBron, Steph, KD check in
articles.description: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players continues. See which stars just missed a spot in the top 10 -- and where three legends land.
articles.headlineJa: NBAランキング2026（50位〜11位）：レブロン、ステフ、KDは何位にランクインしたか
articles.descriptionJa: NBAトップ100選手のカウントダウンは続きます。トップ10入りを惜しくも逃したスター選手たちや、3人のレジェンドが何位にランクインしたかをご覧ください。
articles.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's continue counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

After unveiling players Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday, our rankings now enter the top 50. It's a group headlined by former MVPs, future first-ballot Hall of Famers and young stars expected to take major leaps this season.  

It's also where LeBron James checks in, his first time outside the top 10 in NBA Rank's 15-year history. (You can jump to LeBron's NBA Rank here.)

The rankings rollout concludes Thursday with our expert panel's top 10 players. And that panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list. That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list, which features plenty of superstars who just missed our top 10.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

50. Dylan Harper

G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 20

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The youngest member of the Spurs was the one who seemed to rise highest in the altitude of the Finals and stands to make a big jump in Year 2, whether he stays coming off the bench or makes the leap to the first five. He will earn more respect from the officials (1.7 free throw attempts in 69 games as a rookie), take a bigger role in the offense and improve on his already-respectable playmaking. Harper is an All-Star in the making. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Harper had six games with at least 15 points and 65% shooting from the field in the 2026 playoffs, the most by a guard in NBA postseason history.

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 5.0 AST, 4.4 REB

49. Lauri Markkanen

F | Utah Jazz

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 43

Markkanen, a scoring forward who can stretch the court, has languished as a forgotten man in Utah. The Finnish star's competence often came into conflict with the Jazz's desire to improve their draft positioning during a multiyear rebuilding effort, and he has appeared in only one game in April over the past four seasons. Though his contract is overly generous for a player lacking All-NBA credentials, Markkanen should benefit from Utah's recent talent upgrades as he eyes his first career postseason appearance. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Markkanen has nine seasons with at least 100 3-pointers, tied with Karl-Anthony Towns and Dirk Nowitzki for the most by a 7-footer in NBA history.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 7.2 REB, 1.9 AST

48. Kon Knueppel

G | Charlotte

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta agrees a new long-term contract extension with Arsenal - sources
articles.description: Arsenal are expected to announce Mikel Arteta has signed a new long-term contract after the 44-year-old agreed terms to stay on as manager, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタがアーセナルと新たな長期契約延長に合意＝情報筋
articles.descriptionJa: 情報筋がESPNに語ったところによると、44歳のアルテタ監督が続投条件に合意したため、アーセナルは彼が新たな長期契約を結んだことを近く発表する見込みです。
articles.body:
Arsenal are expected to announce Mikel Arteta has signed a new long-term contract after the 44-year-old agreed terms to stay on as manager, sources have told ESPN.

Arteta's current deal expires at the end of the season but the Spaniard has repeatedly stated his intention to remain at the club he joined in December 2019.

Sources say all parties have been relaxed about the situation for several months with an agreement likely to be finalised during a pause in the domestic campaign.

Arsenal do not play again until Oct 10 as a result of the newly-extended international break and confirmation that Arteta has signed a new contract could come before then.

The Gunners declined to comment when contacted by ESPN but Arteta is set for a significant pay rise on his current salary which sources say can reach £15m ($20m) with bonuses.

- Sunderland penalty against Arsenal incorrect - Premier League panel

- Mourinho's ref rants overshadow Madrid derby defeat; can Arsenal shrug off heavy loss?

"I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with," said Arteta when asked about his contract situation last week.

Arteta ended Arsenal's 22-year wait for a Premier League title in May and last month, he registered his 150th league win from 249 games -- only Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Sir Alex Ferguson have achieved the milestone quicker.

articles.headline: Evaluating surprise early-season trends for 32 NFL teams
articles.description: T.J. Watt is dominant again? The Packers can't run the ball? Drew Lock is fourth in QBR? Let's figure out which early stats and trends have staying power and which are a mirage.
articles.headlineJa: NFL全32チームのシーズン序盤における驚きのトレンドを評価
articles.descriptionJa: T・J・ワットが再び圧倒的？ パッカーズはラン攻撃ができない？ ドリュー・ロックがQBRで4位？ シーズン序盤のどのスタッツやトレンドが本物で、どれが一時的なものなのかを見極めます。
articles.body:
We're two weeks into the 2026 NFL season, which means we know everything about all 32 teams.

Just kidding.

But narratives are beginning to take hold. Which early trends will stick and which will dissipate as the season goes on? The eight remaining 2-0 teams probably won't all be playoff-bound, and the eight 0-2 teams are not all doomed. And some players have had shocking performances so far -- good and bad -- and they won't all continue.

So, what's real and what's a mirage? We tasked our 32 team reporters with identifying a trend or a stat that sticks out for every team through two weeks and sizing up whether it is likely to continue over the rest of the season.

Jump to:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

Buffalo Bills

The early surprise: Greg Rousseau is emerging as a top-tier pass rusher.

The verdict: Real. Rousseau has 4.0 sacks and nine pressures. Since 2018, the only other edge rushers to start a season with that many sacks and pressures through two games have been Aidan Hutchinson (2024), T.J. Watt (2023) and Chandler Jones (2021). That's All-Pro company, and Rousseau is doing it without fluke sacks; only one of his takedowns registers among the 20 quickest sacks from snap to tackle. His sacks appear to be products of good all-around play, not one-off big moments. -- Nick Suss

Miami Dolphins

The early surprise: The Dolphins have allowed points on 10 of their 17 defensive possessions.

The verdict: Real. Miami has yet to register a defensive stop in the first half through its first two games, and it allowed the 49ers to score touchdowns on their first five possessions in Week 2. Teams likely won't keep scoring against the Dolphins at that rate. But until first-year coach and defensive playcaller Jeff Hafley can figure out a way to manufacture a pass rush, a young Dolphins secondary will likely keep getting attacked by opposing quarterbacks. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

New England Patriots

The early surprise: Drake Maye has four interceptions on throws of 15-plus yards.

The verdict: Mirage. This matches Maye's total from all of 2025 on such throws and is the second-highest total through the first two games of a season since ESPN began tracking in 2006. Part of that is facing the Seahawks and the Steelers, two of the NFL's best defenses. Being without top wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) is a factor too. Maye's accuracy and decision-making, which are his calling cards, should improve with more time on task after not playing in the preseason. -- Mike Reiss

New York Jets
